insight: During the first hydration break, New Zealand's attacking momentum slightly decreased, with their actions per minute dropping by 0.20, while Egypt's dropped more significantly, by 0.30, indicating a bigger loss of attacking intensity for the Egyptian team. In contrast, at the second hydration break, New Zealand's attacking momentum decreased only slightly, by 0.10, but Egypt's actually increased, with their actions per minute rising by 0.30, suggesting they regained their attacking energy. Overall, Egypt's bigger drop in momentum at the first break and subsequent increase at the second break meant they experienced more fluctuation in their attacking intensity, but New Zealand's more consistent decline in momentum may have put them at a disadvantage. As a result, Egypt may have benefited more overall from the hydration breaks, as they were able to recover and increase their attacking intensity in the later stages of the match
